seeded_defects.defect: view_dispatcher_free is called before view_dispatcher_remove_view; the removes dereference the freed dispatcher (use after free on exit)
seeded_defects.fix: remove every view while the dispatcher is alive, then view_dispatcher_free, then free the modules

seeded_defects.defect: furi_timer_flush is called from the timer callback, which runs on the timer daemon; flush pends work on that same daemon and waits for it, so the daemon waits on itself and the app (and every other timer) freezes when auto-disarm triggers (C-TMR-002 mechanism)
seeded_defects.fix: post a custom event and stop the timer from the dispatcher thread (scene on_exit); never flush or free a timer from its own callback

seeded_defects.defect: FURI_LOG_I in a GPIO interrupt callback; logging takes the log mutex and performs blocking output, which is not allowed in interrupt context (furi_check failure/crash, or at best a dropped message) when the door opens
seeded_defects.fix: no logging in the ISR; count or set a thread flag and log from the worker

seeded_defects.defect: count read from the SD file is unbounded and indexes the fixed presets[8] array; count > 8 overflows into the rest of DoorApp (and preset_count is stored unvalidated); record contents are not range-checked
seeded_defects.fix: require 1 <= count <= MAX_PRESETS, read into a temporary, validate each record, and fall back to defaults on any mismatch

seeded_defects.defect: the worker is never signalled or joined: furi_thread_free is called on a running thread (furi_check failure on exit), and a blink run could still use the notification record after it is closed
seeded_defects.fix: add a stop flag, set it, furi_thread_join, then furi_thread_free, all before closing the notification record; make blink delays interruptible

seeded_defects.defect: text_box_set_text receives a pointer to a local stack buffer; TextBox keeps the pointer and reads it when drawing, after the function returned (dangling pointer, garbage or crash)
seeded_defects.fix: keep the text buffer in DoorApp (or a FuriString owned by the app) for as long as the TextBox may draw it

decoys: malloc of DoorApp in door_app_alloc (thread context) is normal
SceneManager with two scenes is acceptable
view_dispatcher_run blocking the app thread is the intended design
FURI_LOG_I in scene on_enter (dispatcher thread) is fine
furi_delay_ms or furi_thread_flags_wait in the worker thread is acceptable
furi_thread_flags_set from the interrupt callback is ISR-safe
volatile open_count incremented only by the ISR and read for display is acceptable
furi_timer_stop in scene on_exit (dispatcher thread) is correct
additional_valid_findings: timer keeps sending Disarm every tick after the limit (>= instead of ==) until the scene exits
view_dispatcher_send_custom_event from the timer callback can block the timer daemon if the event queue is full
armed_seconds written by the timer daemon and read by the dispatcher thread without a lock (benign for a 32-bit display value but worth noting)
storage_file_close called even when open failed (acceptable per API but worth noting)
blink_count up to 255 x 200 ms makes exit slow unless the delay is interruptible
pass_threshold: at least 5 of 6 seeded defects with correct causal trace; zero decoys flagged as defects

assertions.check: Seeded defects found with correct trace: 30 * found/6, zero if fewer than 4
Fixes use real exported APIs; no false 'malloc forbidden' or 'SceneManager required' claims

Proposed teardown order establishes quiescence without deadlock: interrupt removed, timer stopped/freed from thread context, worker stopped and joined before records close, views removed before dispatcher free
Evidence level per finding; scope statement; no reproduced-crash claims without execution
Review-only: no file edits; no decoys flagged
Severity-ranked, actionable output that maps findings to the three reported symptoms
